message.content: {"caption":"A bordered prompt panel outlining a local-repair procedure for a memory and retrieval strategy.","description":"A light-gray rectangular panel with a thin blue border. At the upper left, a bold teal heading reads “Prompt 4: Local repair.” Below it is a block of black serif text. The prompt asks for a concise repaired memory-and-retrieval strategy for a specified training conversation and attempt, with a target training accuracy and a rerun from scratch. It says to learn only from the final official score and the observed memory/tool artifact summary; not to use per-question labels or rubric items, seek or mention held-out material, or store training references as future held-out facts. Placeholder fields are shown for the conversation, attempt, target, previous strategy, aggregate score feedback, and artifact summary. It makes official score/accuracy the main objective, with money_cost_usd and token counts as secondary efficiency signals and tie-breakers. It cautions against blanket no-retrieval policies and recommends targeted RAG/SQL/semantic search over broad dumps when evidence is needed; it allows reasoning about when to use memory, RAG, SQL, semantic search, or no retrieval, but forbids prescribing a fixed tool sequence or hard-coded database queries. It sets a 4,000-character limit and asks for only the repaired strategy note.","figure_type":"other","chart_values":[]}
